north_star.definition: Count of independent teams that complete the DotMatch evaluation protocol in a rolling 30-day window.
north_star.why: Completed evaluations measure real workflow use; package downloads alone do not.

metrics.name: Anaconda package downloads
metrics.definition: Cumulative downloads reported for the bioconda/dotmatch package over six months.
metrics.target: Establish a baseline; never use this metric as a standalone adoption claim.
metrics.limitation: Downloads do not identify active projects, unique teams, successful runs, or retention.

metrics.name: PyPI downloads
metrics.definition: Download count for the current package version over the most recent 30-day window.
metrics.target: Establish a baseline and compare with completed evaluations.
metrics.limitation: Mirrors, CI jobs, and repeated installs can inflate the count.

metrics.name: Completed external evaluations
metrics.definition: Teams that complete the intake, run, output review, and scorecard in docs/pilot-program.md.
metrics.source: Approved pilot scorecards; private records may be summarized without exposing assay data.
metrics.target: 5 completed evaluations in the first 90-day push.
metrics.limitation: Requires an approved record or auditable private summary; do not infer from clicks.

metrics.name: Repeat workflows
metrics.definition: Independent teams that run DotMatch in at least two distinct workflows within 90 days.
metrics.target: 2 independent teams in the first 90-day push.
metrics.limitation: A repeat workflow must be recorded with scope; an unmerged example is not evidence.

metrics.name: Accepted external integrations
metrics.definition: Workflow, registry, or reporting integrations accepted outside the DotMatch repository.
metrics.source: docs/workflow-adoption.json with public adoption and evidence URLs.
metrics.target: 1 accepted integration in the first 90-day push.
metrics.limitation: Local wrapper payloads and open issues remain planned until accepted externally.

metrics.name: Documentation-to-install intent
metrics.definition: Unique visitors reaching a documented install or quickstart command divided by tutorial visitors.
metrics.source: Opt-in documentation or homepage analytics, when enabled.
metrics.target: Establish a baseline before setting a conversion target.
metrics.limitation: Analytics are optional; no user-level tracking is required for DotMatch to operate.

decision_rules: Report distribution health separately from external use, retention, and integration acceptance.
Never convert a package download count into a unique-user, active-project, or production-use claim.
A public use statement requires an approved record, a public URL, and a scope note.
Review the north-star count monthly and update the target only after the baseline is recorded.
